subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. CompetitorX)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Johnson <tom.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. CompetitorX)

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today to walk through Acme's requirements and the upcoming vendor bake-off. Below is a quick recap from our discussion and suggested next steps so we all stay aligned. Please reply/edit if I missed anything.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Inconsistent latency at peak traffic (p95 spikes above 300ms on current hosted solution)
- Unit cost per embedding/generation is unpredictable and impacting forecast
- Need for deterministic failures and clear fallbacks for production-critical flows

Business/technical goals for the bake-off:
- Achieve p95 generation latency < 200ms for the set of representative prompts
- Support sustained throughput of ~100 req/s for bursty pipelines
- Maintain semantic relevance/quality on our evaluation set (accuracy benchmark + custom prompts)
- Clear unit cost estimate (tokens + infra) and predictable scaling behavior

Decision criteria you called out:
- Latency (p50/p95), throughput, and tail behavior
- Quality on your core prompt set + few business-critical edge cases
- Integration effort / SDK compatibility with your infra
- Cost per 1M tokens at target throughput
- Security/compliance posture (VPC, auditability)

Proposed bake-off tests (Redwood -> Acme):
1) Latency profile: run representative generation suite (attached) at target concurrencies to capture p50/p95/p99
2) Throughput/stability: 30-minute soak at 100 req/s with KV/cache enabled and disabled
3) Quality eval: run the 150 prompt evaluation set (you can send any additional edge prompts)
4) Failure/fallback behavior: simulate node eviction and ensure graceful fallbacks to smaller variants

Attachments: bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (template we’ll use to capture results)

Timeline & next steps:
- Action: Tom to confirm the final prompt set and provide any additional edge cases — by EOD 6/11
- Action: Acme to provide test credentials or a short-lived API token for test harness — by 6/13
- Redwood to run initial baseline tests and share results + scorecard by 6/16

Primary contacts:
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — I’ll run the bake-off and own coordination
- David Kim (Redwood) — test harness and perf analysis
- Naomi Feldman (Redwood) — solutions lead, will validate quality metrics

If that looks good I’ll prepare the first run next week and loop in my engineering lead for the test execution.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is very helpful and matches my notes. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Cost: we’re looking for a clear cost target — ideally < $X per 1M tokens (I’ll share exact number with procurement offline).
- Benchmarks: latency target is firm at p95 < 200ms for the critical prompt set.
- Stakeholders: I’ve looped in Kyle (platform engineer) and procurement so they have visibility. Kyle will own the API keys and will coordinate with you on network access.

I’ll get the final prompt set to you by EOD Wednesday (6/11) and can provide short-lived test credentials the week of 6/13. One ask: can you include a side-by-side comparison in the scorecard that shows Redwood vs CompetitorX on the same rows (latency, throughput, cost, quality) so we can present to the evaluation committee?

Also: we want to validate semantic drift on a few of our long-context prompts — I’ll flag those in the prompts folder.

Appreciate the timeline. Looking forward to the results.

—Tom

Thanks Marissa / Tom — I’ve put together a first-pass test plan and schedule. High level:

Test plan highlights:
- Environment: isolated test cluster in us-west with identical instance types across vendors
- Latency test: 3 runs of the representative prompt set at concurrencies [5, 25, 100] to capture p50/p95/p99
- Throughput soak: 30-minute run at 100 req/s (observe mem/CPU/GPU utilization, queueing)
- Quality eval: Naomi will run the 150-prompt set; we’ll compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics plus our business scoring rubric
- Failover test: remove one node mid-run and observe fallback latency and error rates

Deliverables & schedule:
- 6/14: dry-run internal only (Redwood) to validate harness and metrics collection
- 6/16: customer-facing runs (Redwood & CompetitorX) — we’ll capture scorecard and raw metrics
- 6/17: results deck + filled scorecard to Acme

Action items for Acme:
- Provide final prompt set and any edge-case prompts (Tom)
- Provide short-lived API token or test creds for the week of 6/13 (Kyle)

Links: test harness repo (internal) — https://git.internal.redwood/repo/bakeoff-harness (will share read-only link once creds are provisioned)

Attachment: test-plan-v1.docx (docx, 24KB)

I’ll queue up the dry-run for 6/14 and share logs. If Acme wants different instance sizing for vendor parity, let us know ASAP.

-David
